::: {#sol-fewest-roads}

Six.
The six roads $\set{a, b}$, $\set{b, c}$, $\set{c, g}$, $\set{g, e}$, $\set{e, d}$ and $\set{e, f}$ are enough:
they join $a$, $b$, $c$, $g$ and $e$ in a row, and $d$ and $f$ to $e$.
Five roads are not enough.
Before any road is built, the seven towns form seven groups of towns that can reach each other.
Each road that is built either joins two towns of the same group, or joins two groups into one,
so after $k$ roads there are at least $7 - k$ groups.
To have only one group, the county needs $7 - k \le 1$, that is, $k \ge 6$.

:::
